title: Proud to Introduce the Casino game Craps based Roguelite I've been making in my spare time: Aleator
author: gmharrison388
selftext:
I've long had the idea to make a roguelite style game based on my favorite casino game craps. Every Bet forces you to make a choice - Either take the winnings, or Sacrifice the win to powerup your table. You have to progress through 7 different tables with difference win conditions on each one, and some of the tables may fight back!

  
My hope is that it is in the Appstore soon!

comments.author: HEXAPONG
comments.body: I'm assuming it is currently web based. Have you began working on packaging it for iOS?

replies.author: gmharrison388
replies.body: It's actually React-native now.  I started originally web based but then transitioned to React Native when the overall design started to come together.

comments.author: EnumeratedArray
comments.body: Sounds like a cool concept, but please consider doing some research and work on UX and UI design before publishing! There's _so much_ text and it's really hard to understand what anything on the screen means.

replies.author: apatosaurios
replies.body: This user interface looks straight out of a spaceship command console!

replies.author: gmharrison388
replies.body: Great Feedback - This is later in the game where I've already powered up the table substantially.  Perhaps I need more images/videos of Early game where it isn't so dense.  I also built a full intro to Craps for people who aren't familiar with the base game.

replies.author: EnumeratedArray
replies.body: Even for a late game this is far too dense. Look at other games in this area like Balatro or Luck Be A Landlord. They add a tonne of complexity into the late game but the UI barely has to change to accomodate it.

comments.author: No-Trouble-9138
comments.body:
Seems like there is something fun there, but I can't barely grasp all that information. It's too dense.

Also make the effects bigger, exaggerated, like.. like a game.

replies.author: gmharrison388
replies.body: Great Feedback - Thank you.  I'm a finance guy by trade so the Art side of things is what I've needed the most help with
